title: Bare Metal Qwen
lede: Phase 2 of the llm.asm project boots Qwen3-0.6B as its own x86-64 operating system, written in assembly with no Linux, C, Rust or libc, straight into a chat prompt.

points: The kernel is a 24 KB static Multiboot image that reaches a multi-turn chat in under 100 ms and keeps the KV-cache between turns.
Weights are bound zero-copy from RAM on 2 MiB huge pages, and inference is spread over every CPU core.
The author reports 134.9 tokens per second decode on 16 vCPUs under QEMU KVM, ahead of llama.cpp CPU Q8_0 in the project's own benchmarks.
It ships as a hybrid BIOS and UEFI ISO that runs on a diskless Proxmox VM, and needs a CPU with AVX2, FMA and F16C.
Output matches the Linux assembly build token for token on five parity prompts.

points.text: One commenter says the OS layer is negligible next to a large model's needs; a reply argues dropping it shrinks the attack surface and adds reliability.
A commenter questions whether the quoted throughput is actually good for a 0.6B model.
Several see it as a step toward the model as the operating system, fronted only by a chat interface.
Others wonder about serving models this way in data centres, though isolation might bring a hypervisor or OS back.
